text:
Friday in Las Vegas showed what Nashville still asks of Roman Josi at 36: 31.7 minutes, his most in ten games, and then the shootout winner that made it seven straight wins, as TSN and others reported. The 2019-20 Norris Trophy winner has 23 points in 20 games, 21 of them assists and 11 on the power play, and he passed 800 career points along the way.

Our numbers split that line in two. The playmaking is real: Nashville's share of five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) is 8.6 points better with him on the ice than off, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 44% of his entries last season. The scoring pace is partly borrowed. The Predators have scored 10.7 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there, and on-ice luck like that fades. His own shot runs the other way: 2 goals on 4.1 expected, a 3.7% shooting rate. If you watch one thing, watch whether the assists keep coming once his teammates' finishing cools.
headline: Roman Josi, 36, still runs Nashville's streak
